title: --cassette absorbs a request whose base URL lost its prefix, hiding the mistake it was meant to catch
foundBy: user report (jsd): "Why do we still need the --cassette option at all?"

evidence.verified: `cs-vcr replay --help` no longer lists --cassette, and a POST to http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/messages with no /c/ prefix returns 404 no_cassette: "the base URL must end in /c/<name> to say which cassette this request belongs to". SPEC R1a now states the refusal and carries the corrected measurement: Claude Code's HEAD /api/hello preconnect builds its URL from ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and so carries the prefix.

details:
A `/c/<name>` prefix on the base URL names the cassette a request belongs to. `--cassette` names one for requests that carry no prefix, and that is the whole of what it now does.

It is a hazard rather than a convenience. Before the prefix mapped to a cassette directly, a request matching no client was refused with `unknown_client`, so that a base URL missing its prefix could not look like it worked while its traffic landed somewhere else. `--cassette` reinstates exactly that failure: forget the prefix and the run records into whatever the session happens to name. With no session cassette either, a recording session proxies everything and records nothing, and only `recorded 0` in the summary says so.

The justification written into SPEC R1a is measurably wrong. It claims the fallback catches requests that cannot carry the prefix, naming Claude Code's `HEAD /api/hello` preconnect, which sets no headers at all. The preconnect builds its URL from `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, so it carries the prefix like everything else: pointing Claude Code 2.1.232 at `http://127.0.0.1:9501/c/probe` produces `HEAD /c/probe/api/hello`. Measured, not inferred.

So the option should go, and a request that names no cassette should be refused and told what its base URL should have ended in.

notes.text: Reviewing the startup checks alongside this found the same rule applied unevenly. A cassette_provider pin naming an unconfigured provider was refused at startup, while default_provider carrying the same typo was not, and neither was a base_url that will not parse. Both matter, and default_provider most: it takes the paths cs-vcr does not model, which is what a client's startup probe hits, so a typo there is a 502 on the first request a session makes.

Replay resolved an upstream before the replay branch, so a session could fail with no_provider for a provider it could never have called. Goal 1 asks a recorded session to replay with no provider reachable and no credential configured; reachable was structural, configured was true only because the default configuration names two providers.

Two documentation defects surfaced while bringing the docs across. CS_VCR_HOME relocates the config file and was documented nowhere, and `record --help` claimed the command serves what the cassette already holds, which is the opposite of what SPEC R3 requires of a recording session.
Closed from the outside during a documentation walkthrough. The flag was already gone and the refusal already in place; the record had been left in flight.
